plates.notes: TRIPLE ELEVATION — three adjoining houses (Nos 36, 38, 40) by one architect, drawn as one plate. THE NEIGHBOUR-ALIGNMENT RESULT: I measured the horizontal edge-energy peaks separately in the left, middle and right thirds of the plate. Every floor line, string course, cornice and roof line matches across all three houses to within 2-5 px (0.05-0.12 m), and the small residual is a uniform tilt of the whole drawing (roof crest 216/213/211 left-to-right, cornice 365/363/360), not a real step. So: adjoining Troisième-classe houses of one build share floor levels EXACTLY, and share the cornice, the two continuous balconies and the roof. The three frontages are also near-identical in width: 8.63 / 8.54 / 8.53 m. WHAT DIFFERS between neighbours is bay count and rhythm, not levels: Nos 36 and 40 carry 3 evenly-spaced bays at 2.69 m pitch; No 38 carries 4 bays in the same frontage, arranged as a symmetric pair-plus-pair (gaps 94.5 / 66 / 96 px) about a central axis, with its entrance door on that axis. The composition is symmetric overall: the extra wall sits at the two outer ends of the group. STOREY COUNT: rez-de-chaussée (shops) + 4 étages + habitable mansard with 3 dormers per house = 6 occupied levels; storey_count=5 counts the masonry storeys only. NO ENTRESOL — the shopfronts are single-height glazing under a deep entablature. TAPER FINDING: the storey heights do NOT taper smoothly. There is one big step (shop 4.01 m → 1er 3.00 m, ratio 0.75), then the 1er/2e/3e are 3.00/3.07/3.00 m, i.e. flat within error, and only the top étage drops to 2.84 m. Any generator constant that applies a per-storey taper of 0.9 or less to each successive storey will be wrong for this class. OPENING FINDING: the window opening is essentially the SAME SIZE at every storey (≈1.10 m wide × 2.1-2.2 m high; h/w 1.9-2.0). The storey height changes; the opening does not. The spandrel/wall band absorbs the difference. 1er-étage opening height could not be confirmed because rolled sun-blinds are drawn across every window head — reported as UNCERTAIN with a lower bound.

plates.notes: Single 5-bay maison à loyer, 12.27 m frontage — rez-de-chaussée with two shopfronts flanking a central entrance, then 4 étages, then a plain low slate roof with NO dormers and no habitable comble. NO ENTRESOL (the shopfronts have a transom band of small panes but no separate floor level). NO PROJECTING BALCONY anywhere: all 20 upper windows carry flush iron garde-corps only. The facade is exactly symmetric about the central bay (facade centre x=905.5, central window centre x=904, door centre x=904.5) and the bay rhythm is NOT uniform: the two inner gaps are 2.57 m and the two outer gaps 2.21 m, so the composition reads 2-1-2 rather than as five equal bays. Same taper finding as the Beaumarchais plate: one step down from the shop storey (3.61 → 3.00 m, ratio 0.83), then 1er and 2e IDENTICAL at 3.00 m, 3e 2.93 m, and only the top storey drops sharply (2.20 m wall height). Same opening finding: opening width is constant at 1.04 m on all four étages, opening height 1.86-2.01 m, h/w 1.79-1.93 — the openings barely change while the storeys do. The two plates agree closely on overall height to cornice (15.64 m here, 15.93 m at Beaumarchais) over the same 5 masonry storeys, from two independently-read scale bars — that is a useful cross-validation of both scales.
